To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common metabolic disturbances and symptoms in patients with chronic kidney failure are hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia and anemia, and that these can be treated with conservative management.

the metabolic alterations and clinical manifestations of chronic kidney disease treated without dialysis are mainly due to retention of nitrogenous and nonnitrogenous waste products, electrolytes and fluids.

the metabolic alterations associated with chronic kidney diseases are hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, anemia, and uremia; and the symptoms that may be present in patients with chronic kidney diseases include pruritus, anorexia, weight loss, fatigue, and insomnia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing the medical community with information on the management of chronic kidney disease patients who refuse dialysis.
the metabolic and clinical manifestations of patients with chronic renal disease, which are not treated with dialysis and the main therapeutic measures that can be adopted in these cases

the following aspects: 1) the main causes of chronic kidney disease; 2) the metabolic alterations and their clinical consequences; 3) the symptoms arising from chronic renal failure; 4) the treatment of the symptoms and 5) the prognosis of patients with advanced chronic kidney disease not undergoing dialysis
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conservative management of patients with chronic renal failure is a complex process, which requires a multidisciplinary approach.
the management of patients with chronic renal failure who refuse dialysis or are unable to have dialysis should be individualized and based on the patient's preferences, values and goals of care.
patients with end stage renal disease who refuse dialysis or cannot receive dialysis should be managed in a palliative care unit with the support of nephrologists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with chronic kidney diseases have the right to choose not to be dialysed.
patients who refuse dialysis should be managed in a multidisciplinary setting with a focus on symptom management, quality of life and end of life care.

patients with chronic kidney diseases are a vulnerable population, and that a multidisciplinary approach with palliative care and end of life care should be implemented in order to improve the care of these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with chronic kidney diseases should be followed by a multidisciplinary team that includes nephrologists, general practitioners, nurses, nutritionists, and social workers.
the metabolic alterations and clinical symptoms associated with chronic kidney failure are not necessarily the same in all cases.
the main symptoms and metabolic disturbances of chronic kidney disease are related to the accumulation of nitrogenous wastes, fluid overload, and electrolyte imbalance.
